title: The adapter changes a newer engine's file before seeing that it is newer, although it says it does not touch it
body: `tryOpen` runs `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` (plus `quick_check`) before `migrate` reads `schema_migrations`. When a newer engine wrote the file in a different journal mode, this rewrites its header (bytes 18-19) and creates `-wal`/`-shm`, which breaks design.md decision 4 ("no toca el fichero") and the notice text at line 109. The test «de una versión más nueva… no toca el fichero» does not catch it, because the file it uses is already in WAL. Fix: open first without changing the mode (or with `readOnly`), check `MAX(version)`, and only then switch to WAL, set the pragmas and migrate. Add a test whose fixture is in `journal_mode = DELETE`.

title: load() loses a strip whose id is `__proto__`, so the SQLite adapter diverges from the memory one
body: `state[stripId] = …` on an object literal calls the `__proto__` setter instead of creating the own key, so `load()` drops a strip with that id. The same happens with `of[String(row.effect_id)]` at line 193. Strip ids come from the config file and are any non-empty string, and the memory adapter (`Object.fromEntries`) keeps the strip, so the two adapters do not meet the same contract. Build both maps with `Object.fromEntries` (or `Object.create(null)`), and add a contract case with that id so it runs against both adapters.

title: The memory adapter accepts states that SQLite rejects (active effect without its values)
body: SQLite enforces through the foreign key that `values` holds the active effect (in this save or an earlier one), and its own test checks that it rejects the save. The memory adapter accepts the same input without complaint. Because the core is meant to be tested against the memory adapter (contract docstring), a core bug that saves `{activeEffect: 'x', values: {}}` would pass in unit tests and throw on the table. Make the memory adapter throw in the same case, and move the «rechaza un efecto activo sin sus valores» test into `describeStateStoreContract` so both adapters run it.

title: ROLLBACK can hide the original error when SQLite has already rolled back
body: With SQLITE_FULL, SQLITE_IOERR or SQLITE_NOMEM, SQLite can roll the transaction back by itself. Then `db.exec('ROLLBACK')` throws «cannot rollback - no transaction is active», and that error replaces the real one, which matters for the log in MOO-130 when a save fails. Guard it with `if (db.isTransaction) db.exec('ROLLBACK')`, or wrap the rollback in its own try so the original error is the one rethrown.

title: Test code inside src/core: it imports vitest and counts as product code
body: The contract file is only test code, yet it sits in `src/core` and imports `vitest`. The coverage `include` (`packages/*/src/**`) and SonarQube therefore count it as product code, and the core source tree takes a dependency on the test framework. Move it to a test-only location (for example `packages/engine/test/`), or exclude it in both vitest.config.ts and sonar-project.properties.
